profile.headline: Principal AI UX/UI Architect | Systems Thinker | Healthcare Enterprise Architecture | Specification-driven Practice Author
profile.summary:
For a decade at Leidos QTC Health Services, I architected UX systems that served over 2 million examinees annually across mission-critical healthcare and benefits platforms - reducing enterprise rework by 92.5% over five years and delivering 99.999% uptime across a design system scaled to 30+ engineering teams.

That work taught me something the field rarely names: the biggest threat to clinical AI is not bad data or weak models, it is confident fallibility. AI that sounds certain when it is wrong. Designing against that requires more than good interface instincts. It requires a principled framework for trust.

Over the past several years I have been building that framework. The result is the Trustworthy AI Interaction Pattern Library 15+ documented design patterns for enterprise and healthcare AI products, covering hallucination mitigation, explainable AI outputs, verifiable citations, human-agent collaboration interfaces, and granular access control. It is the only publicly available pattern library written for regulated AI environments.

My methodology is hybrid by design: OOUX for object modeling in complex domain structures, Atomic Design for component scalability, and Privacy by Design for compliance architecture across HIPAA, WCAG 2.2, FDA SaMD, NIST AI RMF, & GDPR. I apply generative AI: Claude Code, Figma, Lovable, Base44 as build accelerators.

Currently, I am co-authoring applied research with physicians at Penguin AI, developing a cognitive load audit framework for clinical AI interfaces. This work sits at the intersection of human factors analysis, regulatory compliance, and the practical reality of how clinicians make decisions under pressure.

Earlier in my career I led UX for NASA JPL & NSF data platforms at Raytheon, contributed UX strategy to Gov Healthcare Management System Modernization program, and served as part-time Computer Science faculty at Cal State LA, where I mentored senior capstone teams building enterprise-grade AI platforms.

I also run CaliFlyAI Academy, an AI literacy program for non-technical professionals navigating the AI era - because the trust problem in AI is not only a design problem. It is an education problem.

If you are building healthcare AI products that need to be both clinically trustworthy and commercially scalable, I would like to talk.

positions.title: Founder & AI Literacy Lead | LinkedIn, Substack & Podcast
positions.description:
Most people encountering AI for the first time are not non-technical, they are under-served. CaliFlyAI Academy exists to close that gap: affordable, practical AI education built for career mobility and real-world productivity, not credentials.

What we built and what it produced.

Launched a Substack publication and companion podcast that reached 5.3K learners across 118 countries within 90 days, without paid acquisition. The audience is global, self-selecting, and active: professionals in healthcare, education, government, and small business who need AI fluency to remain competitive and found no accessible on-ramp elsewhere.

As founding architect, I owned the full product lifecycle, curriculum design, content system, distribution strategy, and the underlying design system governing AI interaction patterns across the platform. That design system, built on the same OOUX and Privacy by Design principles as my enterprise practice, accelerated content prototyping by an estimated 40% and established a reusable foundation for future course builds.

The translation work here directly informed the Trustworthy AI Interaction Pattern Library: explaining RAG, SLMs, LLMs, MCP, and NLP to non-technical audiences forces a precision that purely technical documentation rarely demands.

Outcomes:
- 5.3K learners · 118 countries · 90 days
- Task completion +60% in tested AI workflow modules
- Privacy by Design and GDPR compliance architecture documented from day one

projects.title: Generative AI & Enterprise Strategy - Blueprinting an Economic Engine via AR/4K-Integrated Urban Revitalization
projects.description: Completed an end-to-end economic development initiative to transform complex civic and community challenges into actionable, user-centric product blueprints for the Lytle Creek neighborhood. This mixed-methods UI/UX innovation began with deep, data-driven analysis—leveraging Caltrans traffic figures and assessor records—to identify strategic opportunities for diversification away from the local economy's extreme reliance on the automotive sector. Applying expertise in Enterprise Content Strategy, I refined proposals into niche, high-ROI concepts, ensuring the final outputs were actionable blueprints, complete with detailed, SEO-friendly content. Crucially, I used my AI Product Design capability, employing context and prompt engineering with generative AI tools, to develop hyper-realistic vision boards for a Specialty RC Hobby Business. This design focused on Compliance-by-Design by utilizing low-impact, infill opportunities (vacant dirt lots) for AR/4K FPV RC tracks, creating a tech-integrated recreational solution for the Commuter & Tech Hobbyist persona. This comprehensive strategy is projected to scale the community by potentially adding 10–20% to the local business count, driving a potential $50 million+ economic impact and creating 500+ jobs by 2030, thus de-risking investment and achieving sustainable community growth.
